Veridian to fill hardware sizing worksheet and share current GPU inventory (by 2025-10-10)
Schedule on-site/air-gap operations walk (2 weeks, tentative)

summary: Discovery call to verify feasibility of deploying Redwood Private in Veridian's sterile (air-gapped) lab environment. Primary concerns: secure offline update process, signed image workflow, hardware constraints (A10 vs A100 capacity, 80GB VRAM needs), patch windows, KMS/HSM integration, audit logs and SSO. Agreement to exchange security docs, hardware inventory, and pilot plan.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-10-02 14:30 PDT | Duration: ~43 minutes
Attendees: Lena Alvarez (Redwood AE), Tomás Reed (Redwood SE), Maria Chen (Redwood SE), Dr. Priya Nair (CTO, Veridian), Ethan Brooks (Infra Lead), Samantha Li (Clinical Ops), Noah Patel (Security)

Auto-summary: feasibility intake for air-gapped cold room deployment. Focus on update delivery, image signing, attestations, patch window and performance sizing for genomics inference workloads.

[00:00] Lena: okay thanks everybody for joining, we'll just do quick intros and then jump in. um one ask up front, is there anything you want on the agenda that i missed?
[00:18] Priya: no that's good, uh high level we want to confirm we can run Redwood Private inside our sterile sequencing lab, full air-gap, can't have outbound connections. And we need a controlled update process, auditability, and predictable inference latency for our variant calling pipeline.
[00:34] Ethan: and hardware details — we have a mix of A10s and a couple of older 40GB cards, plus two new Ampere 80GB nodes arriving next month, so sizing matters.
[00:46] Tomás: great, thanks. quick clarifying q: when you say 'sterile' can you describe update path — do you allow physical media (USB / shipping encrypted images) or is it strictly no external media at all?
[00:56] Samantha: we can bring in sealed media under ops controls. They get scanned, signed, and are transported in chain-of-custody. but no direct internet.
[01:08] Maria: perfect, that matches a lot of our private deployments. we do image signing + manifest verification, and an offline activation flow. we'll walk through the mechanics.

[01:24] Ethan: one concern: how do we apply security patches without internet? our security team has a strict patch window every quarter and requires attestations.
[01:33] Noah: yep we need KMS integration or hardware HSM to store keys and an attestation log that shows which image and key was used.
[01:41] Lena: ok understood. let me outline: Redwood Private provides a control-plane you can host inside a locked network, or we provide a customer-managed control plane image you can run air-gapped. updates are delivered as signed artifacts. In the air-gap scenario we support signed bundle delivery (OCI-like image) that you move via approved media. The node will verify signature using a local KMS/HSM or a key stored in a sealed enclave.
[02:02] Priya: when you say local KMS, do you integrate with HSM vendors? we have a Thales HSM on site.
[02:08] Maria: yes we support external HSM via PKCS#11 and also can work with Vault in sealed mode. for Thales we typically use PKCS bridge, we have done that with other customers.

[02:23] [small crosstalk]
[02:27] Ethan: how about rollback? in a sterile environment we can't risk a bad upgrade. We need atomic swaps and ability to keep a known-good image in the node.
[02:36] Tomás: absolutely. our runtime supports dual-image banks: new image staged then promoted only after health checks and optional canary with a pinned subset of nodes. plus offline health probes report to local logs for auditors.
[02:48] Priya: do those logs meet audit expectations? we need tamper evidence and long-term retention, 7 years for certain artifacts.
[02:56] Noah: also chain-of-custody for the media transfer should be logged.
[03:02] Lena: we produce signed audit logs and a compact proof that can be exported and packaged. retention policies are configurable — for on-prem you manage storage but we support integrations with your archival storage (S3-compatible on-prem). For tamper evidence we timestamp hashes and sign them with the HSM key.

[03:24] Samantha: turning to inference, our pipelines are high throughput but each request is relatively small — variant-region scoring on short sequences, lots of small batch calls. latency consistency matters during clinical batches.
[03:36] Tomás: okay we need to size for tail latency under load. rough question for Ethan — what's your typical token/sequence length and concurrency?
[03:45] Ethan: sequences are 2-4k base pairs, model context mapped to ~1.5k tokens equivalent; we run 50 parallel jobs in peak and expect spikes up to 120.
[03:56] Maria: that maps to memory and KV cache pressure. for a 1.5k seq, some of the large LLMs will need 40-80GB of VRAM depending on quant, and continuous batching can help but only to a point in low-latency needs.
[04:14] Priya: we were thinking of using a pruned open model, maybe 13B quantized, to hit our latency targets. does Redwood have recommendations?
[04:21] Tomás: yes we have a model/cost guide. for strict latency with your concurrency, a 13B quantized 4-bit on an 80GB will usually hit your tail latency goals; on A10s you may need to shard across nodes or use smaller quantized variants. we'll include a recommended quant/profile mapping in the sizing worksheet.

[04:42] [brief pause — someone typing]
[04:47] Ethan: about hardware lifecycle: we can't take nodes offline outside quarterly windows except in emergencies. what's Redwood's suggestion for rolling updates?
[04:55] Lena: we support configurable maintenance windows and can stagger node promotions. for critical security patches that require emergency deploys, we can provide a signed emergency patch artifact and suggested rollback plan. but we'd need your ops sign-off and a special acceptance flow.

[05:12] Noah: also need to understand any telemetry Redwood collects. If the control plane is customer-managed do you still get usage telemetry?
[05:20] Maria: no outbound telemetry from air-gapped control plane unless you opt-in to export artifacts manually. runtime can produce local usage logs, but nothing leaves the network automatically. our hosted API does telemetry in the cloud, but private on-prem is silent by default.

[05:37] Priya: what's the onboarding timeline? we have regulatory timelines — need a pilot and then 6 week go/no-go.
[05:45] Tomás: typical pilot is 4-6 weeks, includes bench tests (throughput/latency), security validation, and a smoke run with your pipeline. we can compress if you provide hardware and key access.

[06:00] Samantha: bench tests — will you run them on our hardware or do you bring reference hardware?
[06:06] Tomás: we prefer to run on your hardware for accurate numbers. if you can't provide, we can run on a partner lab but call it indicative.

[06:16] Ethan: packaging of updates — is there a recommended signing CA process? we have internal CA and root CA for signing images.
[06:24] Maria: supported. we verify chain to a root you control. we also support signed manifests with SHA-256 digests and key rotation.

[06:36] [00:06:40 -> small laughter as someone fumbles an acronym]
[06:41] Priya: encryption at rest and in-transit — we have HSM, and internal S3 for artifacts. we need to ensure model weights never leak.
[06:50] Lena: weights can be stored encrypted and only decrypted inside the node with keys gated by HSM; we also support disk encryption and mlock for memory-resident secrets.

[07:03] Noah: what about RBAC and SSO? we use Okta and need SCIM provisioning, fine-grained role controls, and audit trails per user.
[07:12] Maria: we integrate with Okta SAML and SCIM for user provisioning; RBAC maps to roles in the control plane and you can restrict admin actions to specific groups. we also emit user-action logs for audit.

[07:26] Ethan: can model rollouts be A/B tested internally? we need canary rules for clinical validation.
[07:32] Tomás: yes, we have canary and traffic-splitting policies; on-prem you define the node sets and we can route a percentage or pin experiments to a subset. plus automatic fallback to previous version if regressions are detected.

[07:47] Priya: okay wonderful. a few edge questions from compliance: 1) chain-of-custody for physical media, 2) signed attestation for which HSM key was used, and 3) long-term archival of logs offsite — do you support WORM storage integrations?
[08:01] Lena: chain-of-custody we expect ops to manage but we can generate manifest receipts that travel with the media. attestation is a signed proof we can export. and WORM/S3-compatible archival is supported via your on-prem object store.

[08:20] Samantha: on the operational side — we have a small ops team with limited on-call; how much day-to-day maintenance will this add?
[08:28] Maria: ongoing ops are similar to other on-prem infra: image promotions, occasional reboots, and periodic capacity planning. we can provide automation (playbooks, scripts) and runbook docs. for enterprise customers Redwood also offers a managed ops add-on if you want us to handle updates under your approvals.

[08:47] Ethan: curious about fallback: if a node fails during a clinical run and we have no internet, is there an offline fallback model we can ship on the cluster?
[08:56] Tomás: yes you can pin a smaller, locally-stored fallback model (smaller parameter count) that has lower resource needs; cluster will fallback and continue at reduced capacity. this is common for critical pipelines.

[09:12] Priya: do you support partly-managed topologies where control plane is in our VPC but some non-sensitive telemetry can optionally be pulled to Redwood for business insights?
[09:22] Lena: yes hybrid is possible; the control plane stays in your VPC, and you can opt-in to push anonymized usage bundles over an isolated egress pipe under your control. otherwise everything stays internal.

[09:36] [brief pause, file link referenced]
[09:40] Lena: i'll drop links in the follow-up: sizing worksheet, security pack, and our signed image spec.

[09:45] Ethan: ok about quant and performance — does Redwood offer automated quantization suggestions or toolchains?
[09:51] Maria: yes Redwood Optimize recommends quantization profiles per workload and we can produce model-specific traces. for on-prem we supply the quant artifacts and a reproducible quantization runbook.

[10:03] Priya: any data residency concerns? some lab data must remain within building boundaries. how do you prove data never left the site?
[10:12] Tomás: for air-gapped setups no data leaves unless you export logs manually. for additional assurance we can generate signed proofs of upload attempts (i.e., no outbound attempt was made). we also support local-only telemetry storage and signed attestations.

[10:27] Noah: question from security: if we use an HSM to sign images, how do we handle key rotation without internet?
[10:34] Maria: key rotation is supported; you can rotate local keys via the HSM operator interface and update signing manifests. we document the key rotation process for auditors.

[10:45] Ethan: latency SLA: we're not asking for millisecond, but consistent 95th percentile under 200ms for model inference is a target. feasible?
[10:54] Tomás: on an 80GB A100 or equivalent with the right quant and concurrency tuning, 95p under 200ms for a 13B-ish quantized model might be tight — depends on orchestration and batch patterns. we'll run bench tests to confirm.

[11:12] [mid-call recap by Lena]
[11:14] Lena: recap: 1) you're air-gapped but allow sealed media. 2) need signed image delivery and HSM-based attestation. 3) retention and WORM support for logs. 4) pilot on your hardware for bench tests. we'll send security pack, sizing worksheet, and draft pilot plan. anything to add?
[11:30] Priya: two asks: can you include an explicit chain-of-custody template and an example audit report?
[11:36] Lena: yes.
[11:37] Samantha: and include an estimate of on-call overhead for our ops team, maybe FTE estimate?
[11:41] Maria: we can estimate based on your expected throughput and required SLA. we'll include a couple of staffing scenarios.

[11:49] Ethan: further, can we have a written runbook for emergency rollback steps that we can review with our ops?
[11:55] Tomás: yes we'll draft a runbook and include a checklist for smoke tests pre- and post-deploy.

[12:05] Noah: any legal approvals needed from Redwood beyond an NDA?
[12:08] Lena: after NDA we typically execute a Master Services Agreement for Private deployments; we'll share redlines and a sample SOW for the pilot.

[12:18] Priya: timeline check — if we run pilot in November can we be fully in production by mid-Jan?
[12:25] Tomás: possible, assuming pilot passes and hardware arrives on schedule. we'll refine timeline after we see your inventory.

[12:34] [closing]
[12:36] Lena: cool thanks everyone. i'll shoot the follow-up email with artifacts today and schedule the pilot planning call.
[12:42] Samantha: thanks all, appreciate the clarity.
[12:45] Priya: thanks.
[12:47] Lena: bye.

End of transcript.
